plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: Glossy evergreen shrubs covered in rose-like blooms with golden centers. They flower in the cool, damp weeks when most gardens are bare, so they are a bright surprise in midwinter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn through early spring, peaking in midwinter
plants.location: Japan's mild coastal regions, and winter gardens in the southeastern United States and Europe's Atlantic coast
plants.funFact: Camellia sinensis, a close relative of the Japanese camellia, is the plant that gives us tea.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A dramatic, dinner-plate-sized flower head with a crown of pointed pink bracts around a silky, fuzzy center. It grows in the fynbos scrub of the Southern Hemisphere and is South Africa's national flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mainly late winter to early summer in the wild, with flowers also appearing in the Southern Hemisphere's summer months
plants.location: Western and Southern Cape, South Africa
plants.funFact: Proteas are among the most ancient flowering plants on Earth, and they are adapted to fire. Their thick-walled seed heads protect seeds until a bushfire clears the way for new growth.

plants.name: Hippeastrum puniceum
plants.description: A bold, trumpet-shaped amaryllis relative with large, flared blooms held on tall, sturdy stalks. It flares into color in warm, humid weather.
plants.bloomingSeason: Often blooms in the warm season, with some flowers opening in the Southern Hemisphere's summer
plants.location: Tropical and subtropical Americas, including Brazil and the Caribbean
plants.funFact: Many of the amaryllis sold as winter holiday gifts belong to the genus Hippeastrum, not the true Amaryllis genus.
